During this time, Tappaya became a high-profile fighter on Channel 7 and was ranked first at Lumpini Stadium, although he did not win the belt there.

Throughout his career, Tappaya compiled an impressive record of 200 wins, 36 losses, and five draws, with a Rajadamnern and WMC belt at 61.5 kg, and a no.1 ranking at Lumpini. After his fighting career, Tappaya traveled to China, Japan, and the United Kingdom to teach and compete in Muay Thai, and also competed in kickboxing and MMA in Japan.

In 2009, Tappaya opened his own gym, Sor Klinmee Gym, in Pattaya, Thailand, where he is the owner and acting head trainer. The gym has produced several talented fighters, including Robert Sor Klinmee and Sangpet Sor Klinmee, who regularly compete at major stadiums in Bangkok. Other notable students include Sinsamut Klinmee, Sudsakorn Sor Klinmee, and Thepprasit champion Fasai Sor Klinmee.

Tappaya's achievements in the sport include being a 1997 Rajadamnern Stadium Lightweight Champion and a 1997 WMC World Lightweight Champion. He officially retired from competition in 2001 and has since focused on coaching and running his gym. Today, Sor Klinmee Gym is home to a number of younger boxers, and Tappaya continues to play a significant role in their training and development.

title: Rana Sanaullah
text:
Rana Sanaullah Khan is a Pakistani lawyer and politician who has been serving as Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs since April 2024. He was previously the 39th Interior Minister of Pakistan in the first Shehbaz Sharif government. Sanaullah has been a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan from August 2018 to August 2023 and is a senior member of the PML-N party. He has also served as the president of the PML-N in Punjab since May 2019.

Born on January 1, 1955, in a Punjabi Rajput family, Sanaullah received a bachelor's degree in commerce from Government College University Faisalabad and an LLB from Punjab Law College, Lahore. He is a cousin of former Chief Justice of Pakistan Iftikhar Chaudhry. Sanaullah's political career began in 1990 when he was elected to the Provincial Assembly of Punjab as a candidate of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP). He later joined the Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz) (PML-N) and has been elected to the Provincial Assembly of Punjab multiple times.

Sanaullah has held various high-ranking positions in the province, including Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister of Punjab, Local Governments and Community Development Minister of Punjab, Revenue Minister of Punjab, and Public Prosecution Minister of Punjab. He was also the Deputy Leader of the Opposition in the Punjab Provincial Assembly on two occasions. In 2018, Sanaullah was elected to the National Assembly of Pakistan and was appointed as the Interior Minister in April 2022.

Sanaullah's tenure as Interior Minister was marked by several controversies, including allegations of links with militant organizations such as the Sipah-e-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP). He was also accused of being involved in the disappearance of American contractor Warren Weinstein, who was later killed in a US drone strike. Additionally, Sanaullah was criticized for his role in the Model Town incident, which resulted in the deaths of several people.

In 2019, Sanaullah was detained by the Anti Narcotics Force (ANF) on allegations of drug trafficking. He was later acquitted in December 2022 after a special court in Lahore exonerated him. Sanaullah claimed that the case against him was "concocted, designed, and created" for political reasons.

Throughout his career, Sanaullah has been involved in several controversies, but he has maintained that he has been a victim of political victimization. Despite these challenges, he remains a senior member of the PML-N party and a key figure in Pakistani politics. Sanaullah's recent appointment as Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs is a testament to his continued influence in Pakistani politics.

title: Karni Liddell
text:
Karni Liddell is an Australian Paralympic swimming competitor who was born on March 1, 1979, in Rockhampton, Queensland. At a young age, she was diagnosed with Spinal Muscular Atrophy, a rare neuromuscular wasting disease. For 40 years, she was misdiagnosed, but in 2019, a whole genome sequencing test in Europe revealed that she actually has Congenital Titinopathy, another type of neuromuscular wasting disease. This diagnosis was the result of a 12-year search by Liddell and her family, who had been seeking answers for years.

Growing up, Liddell's doctors predicted a bleak future, telling her parents that she would never be able to walk and would not live past her teens. However, Liddell defied these predictions, achieving great success in swimming. By the age of 14, she had already broken a swimming world record. She went on to compete in two Paralympic Games, in 1996 and 2000, winning medals at both events. In 2000, she was even named the Australian Swimming Team Captain at the Sydney Paralympic Games.

In addition to her swimming career, Liddell has also worked as a radio presenter for 4BC. In 2015, she was one of 18 Australian Paralympians who posed nude for a calendar, photographed by Emma Hack. Liddell's photo showed her wearing sunglasses and body paint designed to look like a polka-dotted bikini. Her image was also one of several painted by Ludmila Clark and displayed at the Customs House in Rockhampton in 2008.

Liddell's journey to diagnosis was lengthy, traumatic, and expensive for her family. However, her determination and resilience have inspired many. Despite the challenges she has faced, Liddell has achieved great success in her swimming career and has become a role model for others. Her story highlights the importance of accurate diagnosis and the need for continued research into rare and complex conditions like Congenital Titinopathy.

title: Ronaldinho
text:
Ronaldinho, born Ronaldo de Assis Moreira on March 21, 1980, is a Brazilian former professional footballer widely regarded as one of the greatest players of all time. He played as an attacking midfielder or left winger and was known for his exceptional dribbling skills, free-kick accuracy, and ability to score and create goals. Throughout his career, Ronaldinho won numerous accolades, including two FIFA World Player of the Year awards and a Ballon d'Or.

Ronaldinho began his career at Grêmio in 1998, making his senior debut during the 1998 Copa Libertadores. He quickly gained recognition for his skills, scoring 22 goals in 47 matches in 1999. His performances caught the attention of European clubs, and in 2001, he signed with Paris Saint-Germain in a €5 million transfer. During his time with PSG, Ronaldinho won the UEFA Intertoto Cup and was praised for his performances, despite controversy with the team's manager.

In 2003, Ronaldinho joined Barcelona in a €30 million deal, where he spent his peak years and gained global fame. He made his Barcelona debut in a friendly against Juventus and scored his first competitive goal in La Liga against Sevilla. Ronaldinho's success with Barcelona was immense, winning the 2004-05 La Liga title and the 2005-06 UEFA Champions League. He was named FIFA World Player of the Year for the second consecutive year and won the Ballon d'Or in 2005.

Ronaldinho's performances were not limited to his club career. He earned 97 caps and scored 33 goals for Brazil, representing them in two FIFA World Cups. He was an integral player in Brazil's 2002 FIFA World Cup-winning team and captained the team to the 2005 FIFA Confederations Cup title. Ronaldinho also won the Copa América with Brazil in 1999 and a bronze medal in men's football at the 2008 Summer Olympics.

In addition to his club and international success, Ronaldinho accumulated numerous individual awards, including three UEFA Team of the Year and FIFA World XI appearances. He was named UEFA Club Footballer of the Year for the 2005-06 season and South American Footballer of the Year in 2013. Ronaldinho was also voted World Player of the Decade 2000s, ahead of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

Throughout his career, Ronaldinho played for several clubs, including AC Milan, Flamengo, Atlético Mineiro, Querétaro, and Fluminense. He won the 2010-11 Serie A with AC Milan and the 2013 Copa Libertadores with Atlético Mineiro. Ronaldinho's legacy extends beyond his on-field accomplishments, as he is credited with changing Barcelona's history and inspiring a new generation of footballers.

Ronaldinho's personal life was marked by tragedy when his father passed away when he was just eight years old. His brother, Roberto, acted as his manager, and his sister, Deisi, worked as his press coordinator. Ronaldinho's nickname "O Bruxo" or "The Wizard" was given to him due to his exceptional skills on the field.

Overall, Ronaldinho's career was marked by incredible success, individual awards, and a lasting impact on the sport. His legacy continues to inspire footballers and fans around the world.

title: Chris Duffield
text:
Christopher Paul Duffield, born on May 20, 1952, is a former Town Clerk of London and Chief Executive of the Corporation of the City of London. He was born to Jack and Irene Duffield and educated at St Albans School in Hertfordshire, before graduating from Newcastle University in 1973 with a Bachelor of Arts degree. Duffield has been involved in local government for nearly 30 years, having worked for various organizations including the GLC, Redbridge, Essex, and Bexley Council, where he held the position of Chief Executive.

In September 2003, Duffield joined the Corporation of the City of London as the Town Clerk and Chief Executive, a position he held until his retirement in 2012, when he was succeeded by John Barradell. As Town Clerk and Chief Executive, Duffield's responsibilities included the efficient management and execution of City functions, serving as primary advisor on policy and resources, and overseeing various City departments such as public relations, economic development, and human resources. He was also responsible for investigating complaints against the City and served as the Electoral Registration Officer.

In addition to his role as Town Clerk and Chief Executive, Duffield was also the chief executive of the Police Authority, overseeing the Police Authority's staff and working closely with the chairman to facilitate an efficient and effective police service within the City of London. Duffield's other responsibilities included servicing meetings of the Court of Common Council and designated committees, as well as the Court of Alderman and designated committees.

Duffield is a member of the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy (CIPFA), which reflects his professional background in public finance. Outside of work, Duffield is a family man, being married with three sons, Mark, Jack, and Joe, and four grandchildren, Amelia, Alex, Katie, and Stanley. He also has a brother, Ian Duffield, and two nieces, Paul Duffield and Melanie Duffield. Throughout his career, Duffield has demonstrated a long-standing commitment to public service, and his work with the Corporation of the City of London has had a lasting impact on the city's governance and administration.

title: Ted Mack (politician)
text:
Edward Carrington Mack, known as Ted Mack, was a prominent Australian politician and architect who made history by becoming the only person to be elected and re-elected as an independent to local, state, and federal governments in Australia. Born on December 20, 1933, in Sydney, Mack completed his education at Sydney Boys High School and later graduated with a Bachelor of Architecture from the University of New South Wales in 1958. He trained as an architect and worked on various projects, including hospitals and public housing, before venturing into politics in 1974.

Mack's entry into politics was sparked by his concern over the construction of a 17-storey office block near his residence in North Sydney. He ran for election to the North Sydney Municipal Council in 1974 and was successful, later becoming the mayor in 1980. During his tenure as mayor, Mack introduced open government policies, making all council meetings, committees, and files open to the public. He also established precinct committees, public meetings, and referendums, which increased public participation in decision-making.

In 1981, Mack decided to run as an independent for the New South Wales Legislative Assembly seat of North Shore, despite it being considered a safe Liberal seat. He won the election, defeating the state opposition leader Bruce McDonald, and was re-elected in 1984 and 1988. Mack's victory was significant, as he was the first independent to win a seat in the New South Wales Parliament.

Mack abruptly retired from politics in 1988, just two days short of serving seven years in parliament, to avoid receiving a parliamentary pension. He spent 18 months out of politics, mainly camping in the outback, before winning the federal seat of North Sydney in 1990. This victory was significant, as it marked the first time an independent had won a federal seat from a major party in Australia.

As a federal MP, Mack opposed unilateral tariff removal, privatization, and Australian involvement in the Gulf War. He was the only MP to vote against the war, and his speech on January 22, 1991, was critical of the government's decision. Mack also introduced a private member's bill for citizen-initiated referendums, similar to those practiced in Switzerland.

Mack chose to retire from federal parliament at the 1996 election, again to avoid receiving a parliamentary pension. After his retirement, he remained active in public life, serving as an independent Republican delegate to the Australian Constitutional Convention and opposing the model favored by the Australian Republican Movement. He was also elected as one of the National Living Treasures in 1997.

In 2015, Mack re-entered the federal political arena by supporting independent candidate Stephen Ruff in the North Sydney by-election. Mack was critical of the Liberal Party's handling of the preselection process and the shortened timeline for nominations.

Mack was diagnosed with terminal brain cancer in 2016 and passed away on November 6, 2018, after suffering a stroke. He was remembered for his commitment to public service, his advocacy for open government, and his dedication to representing the interests of his constituents. In 2019, the Mayor of North Sydney officially renamed the park next to North Sydney Council Chambers as "Ted Mack Civic Park" in his honor.

title: Daniil Medvedev
text:
Daniil Medvedev is a Russian professional tennis player who has achieved great success in his career. Born on February 11, 1996, in Moscow, Russia, Medvedev began playing tennis at the age of six and quickly developed a passion for the sport. He was coached by Ekaterina Kryuchkova, a former coach of professional tennis player Vera Zvonareva, and later trained at the tennis academy in Antibes, France.

Medvedev's early life and education played a significant role in shaping his tennis career. He studied physics and maths at a specialized school before graduating early and enrolling in economics and commerce at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations. However, he dropped out to focus on tennis and later switched to the Russian State University of Physical Education, Sport, Youth, and Tourism, where he received his diploma as a coach.

In his junior career, Medvedev had a win-loss record of 109-43 and won several titles, including six titles in 2012-2013. He made his junior Grand Slam debut at the 2013 Junior Wimbledon and reached the second round. Medvedev's junior career was marked by his impressive performance, and he reached a career-high junior ranking of world No. 13.

Medvedev turned pro in 2015 and made his ATP Tour main draw debut at the 2015 Kremlin Cup. He won his first ATP singles title in 2018 at the Sydney International, defeating Alex de Minaur in the final. Medvedev's breakthrough year was 2019, when he reached six consecutive tournament finals, including the US Open, where he was defeated by Rafael Nadal. He also won two Masters titles that year, in Cincinnati and Shanghai.

In 2020, Medvedev won the ATP Finals, defeating Dominic Thiem in the final. He became the first player to defeat the top three players in the world en route to the year-end championship title. Medvedev's success continued in 2021, when he won his first Grand Slam title at the US Open, defeating Stefanos Tsitsipas in the final. He also led Russia to the title in the ATP Cup, going 4-0 in singles.

Medvedev's personal life has also been a subject of interest. He married his girlfriend Daria Chernyshkova in 2018, and they have two daughters, Alisa and Vika. Medvedev is known to be fluent in French and English, besides his native Russian. He is a supporter of FC Bayern Munich and has credited his marriage for the improvement of his tennis results.

Throughout his career, Medvedev has been known for his aggressive playing style and his ability to perform under pressure. He has won 20 ATP Tour-level singles titles and has been ranked as world No. 1 in men's singles by the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP). Medvedev's achievements have made him one of the most successful Russian tennis players in recent history, and he continues to be a dominant force in the sport.

title: Giorgi Papunashvili
text:
Giorgi Papunashvili, commonly known as Papu, is a Georgian professional footballer born on September 2, 1995. He plays as a winger for Azerbaijani club Zira and has represented the Georgian national senior and youth teams. Papunashvili started his career at Dinamo Tbilisi, his hometown club, where he made his debut in 2013 against Tskhinvali. During the 2014-2015 season, he became a key player, scoring 16 goals in all tournaments, including a hat-trick against Tskhinvali and two goals in the Georgian Cup final against Samtredia, which Dinamo won.

In the summer of 2015, Papunashvili signed a season-long loan deal with Werder Bremen, but his spell was unsuccessful due to injuries that kept him out for 12 games. He made 20 appearances for the club, scoring two goals. In June 2017, he signed a four-year deal with Real Zaragoza, making his debut against Granada CF. Papunashvili played for Zaragoza until January 2020, when he joined Racing de Santander on loan until the end of the season.

Papunashvili's subsequent moves included a transfer to Cypriot club Apollon Limassol FC in December 2020, a return to Erovnuli Liga with Torpedo Kutaisi in January 2022, and a stint with Serbian side Radnički Niš. In March 2023, he signed with Samtredia, and four months later joined Telavi. However, he soon moved to Azerbaijan Premier League side Kapaz and, in August 2024, signed a 1+1 year contract with Zira.

At the international level, Papunashvili made his debut for the Georgian national team in a friendly loss to the United Arab Emirates in June 2014. He also represented Georgia's under-17 team in the 2012 UEFA European Under-17 Championship, scoring a memorable goal against England in the qualifying stage. Throughout his career, Papunashvili has won several honors with Dinamo Tbilisi, including the Umaglesi Liga, Georgian Cup, and Georgian Super Cup.

title: Nancy Onyango
text:
Nancy Asiko Onyango is a Kenyan accountant, businesswoman, and corporate executive who has held various high-profile positions in her career. She was appointed as the Director of the Office of Internal Audit and Inspection at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in December 2017, taking effect in February 2018. Prior to her appointment at the IMF, Onyango served as the CEO of Reliance Risk Advisory Solutions, a Nairobi-based consultancy firm.

Born in Kenya, Onyango pursued her higher education in the country, attending the University of Nairobi (UoN) for her undergraduate and master's degrees. She earned a Bachelor of Commerce degree in Accounting and Finance in 1987 and a Master of Business Administration degree in 1989, both from UoN. She later earned a Doctor of Business Administration degree from the United States International University Africa in 2016, after taking courses at Columbia Business School in New York City.

Onyango has had a long and distinguished career in accounting and consultancy. She worked at PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) in London and Nairobi, rising through the ranks to become a partner and lead the consulting unit at PwC East Africa. She specialized in technology, governance risk, and compliance, and later headed the Risk Assurance Services Unit at PwC East Africa. In 2015, she joined Ernst & Young as a partner and head of governance, risk, and compliance for the African continent.

In addition to her work in the private sector, Onyango has also held various board appointments. She is a non-executive director of Kenya Commercial Bank Group, Cytonn Investments, and Fairtrade Africa, where she chairs the board's audit and finance committee. She is also a married mother of three sons.

Throughout her career, Onyango has demonstrated her expertise in accounting, consultancy, and leadership. Her appointment to the IMF reflects her reputation as a skilled and experienced professional in her field. With her extensive experience in the private sector and her various board appointments, Onyango is well-positioned to make a significant impact in her role at the IMF. Her background and education have provided her with a strong foundation in accounting and business, and she has built a successful career in Kenya and beyond. Overall, Nancy Onyango is a highly accomplished professional who has made significant contributions to the fields of accounting, consultancy, and leadership.

title: Alexander Vovin
text:
Alexander Vovin was a renowned linguist and philologist who made significant contributions to the study of East Asian languages, particularly Japanese, Korean, and Ainu languages. Born on January 27, 1961, in the Soviet Union, Vovin earned his Master's degree in structural and applied linguistics from Saint Petersburg State University in 1983 and his Ph.D. in historical Japanese linguistics and premodern Japanese literature from the same university in 1987.

Vovin's academic career spanned several institutions and countries. He began as a Junior Researcher at the St. Petersburg Institute of Oriental Studies from 1987 to 1990. He then moved to the United States, where he held various positions at the University of Michigan, Miami University, and the University of Hawaiʻi, where he became a full professor in 2003. During his time at the University of Hawaiʻi, Vovin also served as a visiting professor at several institutions, including the International Research Center for Japanese Studies in Kyoto, Japan, and the Ruhr University Bochum in Germany.

In 2014, Vovin joined the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (EHESS) in Paris, France, as the Director of Studies. He was also involved in several research projects, including the Etymological Dictionary of the Japonic Languages, which was funded by the European Union. Vovin's research focused on Japanese historical linguistics, Japanese philology, and the study of Inner Asian languages and Kra-Dai languages. He was particularly interested in the etymology, morphology, and phonology of the Japanese language, as well as the study of the Ainu language and Old and Middle Korean texts.

One of Vovin's notable projects was the translation of the Man'yōshū, a premodern Japanese poetic anthology, into English. He was working on this project until his death, and his work on this text, as well as his research on the Bussokuseki no Uta of Yakushi-ji temple in Nara, was published in 2021. Vovin's other notable works include his research on the relationship between the Japonic languages and other languages, such as Korean and Tungusic.

Vovin was married twice, first to Varvara G. Lebedeva-Vovina, with whom he had a son, Aleksei, and then to fellow Japanese language researcher Sambi Ishisaki, with whom he had two more children. He passed away on April 8, 2022, at the age of 61, due to cancer. A festschrift was dedicated to Vovin on his 60th birthday, and his legacy continues to be celebrated through his contributions to the field of linguistics and philology.

Throughout his career, Vovin published numerous books and articles on linguistics and philology, including "A Reconstruction of Proto-Ainu" and "A Reference Grammar of Classical Japanese Prose". His work has been widely recognized, and he was a respected figure in the field of East Asian language studies. Vovin's research has shed new light on the history and development of the Japanese language, and his work continues to be an important resource for scholars in the field.

title: David Bogue
text:
David Bogue was a Scottish nonconformist religious leader born on February 18, 1750, at Hallydown Farm in the parish of Coldingham, Berwickshire, Scotland. He was the son of John Bogue, a farmer, and his wife, Margaret Swanston. Bogue received his early education in Eyemouth and later studied Divinity at Edinburgh University. He was licensed to preach by the Church of Scotland, but was unable to find a patron in Scotland and was sent to London in 1771 to teach in schools.

In London, Bogue established an institution for preparing men for the ministry in 1771, which would eventually grow into the London Missionary Society. He settled as minister of the independent Congregational church at Gosport in Hampshire in 1777. Bogue was involved in various missionary efforts and was a pioneer in the field of Protestant missions. He was instrumental in preparing missionaries for work abroad, including Robert Morrison and William Milne, who became the first two Protestant missionaries to China.

Bogue's own plans to go to India as a missionary in 1796 were thwarted by the opposition of the East India Company. However, he continued to be involved in missionary work and taught several notable students, including Samuel Dyer, who went on to become a missionary in Penang. Bogue was also a prolific writer and published several works, including "Reasons for Seeking a Repeal of the Test Acts" and "A History of the Dissenters, from the Revolution of 1688 to 1808".

In addition to his work as a minister and writer, Bogue was also involved in founding several organizations, including the British and Foreign Bible Society and the Religious Tract Society. He was awarded a doctor of divinity degree from Yale University in 1815. Bogue died on October 25, 1825, in Brighton, during the London Missionary Society's annual tour.

Throughout his life, Bogue was committed to spreading Christianity and promoting missionary work. His legacy continued to inspire future generations of missionaries and Christian leaders. His contributions to the field of Protestant missions and his role in establishing the London Missionary Society have made him a notable figure in the history of Christianity. Bogue's writings, including his "History of Dissenters" and "Essay on the Divine Authority of the New Testament", remain important works in the field of theology and church history.

title: Cobhams Asuquo
text:
Cobhams Asuquo is a Nigerian musician, producer, and songwriter born on January 6, 1981. He began his academic training as a lawyer, but later pursued a career in music. Asuquo started his music career in the early 2000s, producing hits such as "Maintain in India" and "Catch cold" by Maintain, "Ego" by Djinne, and "In the music" and "If you ask me" by Omawumi. Asuquo has worked with numerous musicians, both locally and internationally, including ASA, Banky W, Omawumi, Eldee, Sasha, Dare Art-Alade, Waje, Timi Dakolo, Djinne, Faze, Seyi Shay, Korede Bello, Tiwa Savage, Ego, Yemi Alade, Bez, Omolara, Chidinma Ekile, Shola Allyson, Lara George, Silver Saddih, Flavour, Mo'Chedda, Praiz, Simi, and Rooftop MC's. In addition to his music production work, Asuquo has also composed and arranged film scores for conservatoires, film, and stage performances. He has performed at international music events, including The Harare International Festival of Arts, the AFA Sponsored French Cultural Center Concert with Asa and Angelique Kidjo, and the launch of MTV's one hundredth channel (MTV Base Africa) in Abuja, Nigeria.

He performed live on stage at the Global Citizens Festival New York Central Park to promote the UN Global Goals. In 2014, he performed at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, and was interviewed by CNN Africa Voices.

Asuquo is visually impaired and has been married to Ojuolape Veronica Olukanni since December 2, 2010. They have two sons together. In 2016, he started a digital radio countdown show, "The Top 12 Countdown with Cobhams Asuquo", which counts down the hottest African/Nigerian songs. Asuquo has released several singles, including "Ordinary People", "Do the Right Thing" featuring Bez, "Star of Wonder", "Boosit" featuring Falz, "The Other Room" featuring Ugovinna, and "Adore" featuring Lauretta Cookey and Fome Peters. His latest single, "We Plenti" featuring Simi, was released on January 6, 2019.

title: Minako Honda
text:
Minako Honda, born Minako Kudo on July 31, 1967, was a Japanese idol and musical singer. Her early life was marked by a passion for singing, encouraged by her mother. As a child, she wrote in her graduation collection that she would like to become an actress or singer. Her interest in music led her to audition for Star Tanjō!, a TV show that aimed to discover new talents. Although she didn't win the competition, her talent was noticed by Bondo Kikaku, a record label that was recruiting a new member for the group Shojotai.

In 1984, Honda performed at the Nagasaki Kayo Festival, a television contest for new idols, and won the Grand Prix for her powerful voice and singing ability. This success led to her debut as a solo artist under the name Minako Honda with the single "Satsui no Vacane" in 1985, for which she received a Japan Record Award for best new artist of that year. Her subsequent releases, including "1986 nen no Marilyn", sparked controversy due to her suggestive performances, which were unusual for an idol at that time.

Throughout her career, Honda attempted to revive her popularity, including forming an all-girl rock group called "Minako with Wild Cats" in 1988. Although the group disbanded a year later, Honda continued to pursue her music career. In 1990, she auditioned for the Tokyo production of the Broadway play Miss Saigon and won the role of Kim, beating out over 15,000 other candidates. Her performance in the play marked a turning point in her career, and she went on to perform in leading roles in other musicals, including Fiddler on the Roof, The King and I, and Les Misérables.

In addition to her theater work, Honda also released several classical albums, showcasing her soprano voice, and sang theme songs for anime programs. Her song "Tsubasa" is notable for its 30-second long note. In 2004, she added a period to her name, believing it would bring her a sense of maturity.

In late 2004, Honda fell ill with symptoms that initially seemed like a cold, but her condition worsened, and she was diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia on January 5, 2005. Despite undergoing treatment, her condition relapsed, and she developed lung complications on October 21, 2005. She lapsed into a coma on November 3 and passed away at 4:38 a.m. on November 6, 2005, at the Juntendo University Hospital in Bunkyō, Tokyo, at the age of 38.

Throughout her life, Honda released 14 original albums, 5 compilation albums, and 25 physical singles, among other works. Her legacy as a talented singer and performer continues to be celebrated by her fans. Her posthumous releases have allowed her music to reach new audiences, ensuring her memory lives on.

title: Don Beard
text:
Don Beard was a New Zealand cricketer who played in four Test matches for his country between 1952 and 1956. Born on January 14, 1920, Beard grew up in the countryside near Palmerston North, where he attended Palmerston North Boys' High School, cycling 15 miles a day to get there. After completing his teacher training in Auckland, he went on to study at Victoria University in Wellington, where he earned a Diploma in Education in 1946 and a Master of Arts degree in 1948. His Master's thesis was on the history of physical education in New Zealand primary schools.

Beard was an accurate fast-medium bowler and a useful lower-order batsman who played first-class cricket for several teams, including Wellington, Central Districts, and Northern Districts. He made his first-class debut in 1945, but had to wait until 1950-51 to play in the Plunket Shield, which he did for Central Districts in their inaugural match. In the 1951-52 season, Beard took 16 wickets at an average of 27.25, earning him a spot in the New Zealand team for two Tests against the touring West Indies side, where he took four wickets.

Beard's international career was marked by some notable performances, including a match-winning effort in the Fourth Test against the West Indies in 1956, where he took 1 for 20 and 3 for 22 and helped New Zealand secure their first-ever Test victory. He also played a crucial role in a match against Central Districts, where he top-scored in each innings, making 25 and 67, and took 3 for 52 and 2 for 59.

In addition to his cricket career, Beard was a schoolteacher and school principal. He became the principal of Te Aroha College in Waikato in 1961 and continued to play cricket for several years, including a few games for Northern Districts. Beard's cricket career was marked by several notable performances, including a best match haul of 11 wickets against Otago in 1956-57.

Beard was a tall man, standing nearly six feet three inches, and was also a talented sportsman in other disciplines. He played basketball for New Zealand, was a notable amateur golfer, and played rugby union for Wellington, Wanganui, and North Island. After retiring as principal of Te Aroha College, Beard went on holiday to England, where he died on July 15, 1982. His son Derek also went on to play first-class cricket in New Zealand. Throughout his life, Beard was known for his athletic ability and his dedication to sports and education.

title: PewDiePie
text:
Felix Arvid Ulf Kjellberg, better known as PewDiePie, is a Swedish YouTuber and comedian. He was born on October 24, 1989, in Gothenburg, Sweden, to Lotta Kristine Johanna and Ulf Christian Kjellberg. Growing up, PewDiePie was interested in art and video games, and he spent much of his childhood playing games on his Super Nintendo Entertainment System and creating artwork. He attended high school in Gothenburg, where he developed a passion for video games and began to create Let's Play videos.

PewDiePie's YouTube channel, "PewDiePie," was created in 2010, and he initially focused on creating Let's Play videos of horror and action games. His channel gained popularity rapidly, and by 2012, he had become one of the fastest-growing YouTubers. He signed with Maker Studios in December 2012, a multi-channel network that helped him grow his channel. However, PewDiePie has spoken about feeling neglected by Machinima, a rival network, and has credited his success to his ability to adapt to the ever-changing landscape of YouTube.

In 2013, PewDiePie's channel became the most-subscribed on YouTube, surpassing Smosh. He received a Guinness World Record certificate for the achievement. Throughout 2012 and 2013, his channel was one of the fastest-growing on YouTube, and he became known for his commentary and humor. PewDiePie's content has been praised for its entertainment value, and he has been credited for helping to popularize the Let's Play genre.

However, PewDiePie's content has also been criticized for its polarizing reception. PewDiePie responded to the criticism, stating that his content was taken out of context and that he was not a racist or anti-Semitic.

Despite the controversy, PewDiePie remained one of the most popular YouTubers. He continued to create content, including Let's Play videos, vlogs, and comedy sketches. PewDiePie has also been praised for his charity work, including his support for the ALS Association and the Make-A-Wish Foundation.

In 2018 and 2019, PewDiePie engaged in a public competition with Indian record label T-Series to become the most-subscribed channel on YouTube. However, he ultimately lost the title to T-Series. PewDiePie has spoken about the stress and pressure of maintaining his channel, and has stated that he has considered retiring from YouTube.

Today, PewDiePie is semi-retired from YouTube, and he uploads videos less frequently. He has moved to Japan with his wife, Marzia, and has stated that he focuses on creating content for his own enjoyment rather than for career purposes. Despite his decreased activity, PewDiePie's channel remains one of the most-subscribed and viewed on YouTube, with over 110 million subscribers and 29.4 billion views. He has been named one of Time magazine's 100 most influential people in the world and has been recognized for his influence on Internet culture.

PewDiePie's legacy is complex and multifaceted. He has been credited with helping to popularize the Let's Play genre and has been praised for his entertainment value. However, he has also been criticized for his content and has faced backlash for his actions. Despite this, PewDiePie remains one of the most popular and influential YouTubers, and his impact on the platform and Internet culture as a whole is undeniable.

title: Jeremy Northam
text:
Jeremy Northam is an English actor born on December 1, 1961, in Cambridge, Cambridgeshire. His father, John Northam, was a professor of literature and theatre. Northam studied English at Bedford College, London, and acting at the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, and is also an alumnus of the Royal Holloway, University of London.

Northam began his career on screen and stage, making his television debut in the series "American Playhouse" as Mr. Benson in the episode "Suspicion". He went on to appear in various British television shows and films, including "Wish Me Luck" (1987) and "Piece of Cake" (1988). On stage, he performed at the Royal National Theatre, where he replaced Ian Charleson and Daniel Day-Lewis in the role of Hamlet in 1989. For his performance in "The Voysey Inheritance", he won the 1990 Laurence Olivier Award for Best Newcomer in a Play.

Northam's film career took off in the mid-1990s, with notable roles in "The Net" (1995), his American film debut, "Carrington" (1995), "Emma" (1996), "Amistad" (1997), "An Ideal Husband" (1999), and "The Winslow Boy" (1999). He also appeared in "Gosford Park" (2001) as Welsh actor and singer Ivor Novello, and in "Enigma" (2001). In 2002, he starred in the film "Cypher", and in 2004, he portrayed golfer Walter Hagen in "Bobby Jones: Stroke of Genius".

In television, Northam played Thomas More in the Showtime series "The Tudors" from 2007 to 2008. He also appeared as Anthony Eden, the British Prime Minister, in the Netflix series "The Crown" from 2016 to 2017. His other notable roles include John Brodie Innes in the 2009 film "Creation", and Bertrand Russell in the 2015 film "The Man Who Knew Infinity".

In addition to his screen work, Northam has also done audiobook work, narrating titles such as "The Silver Chair" by C.S. Lewis, and "The Great Poets" by Gerard Manley Hopkins. He has also recorded works by Henry James, George Orwell, and Graham Greene. Northam was married to Canadian film and television make-up artist Liz Moro from 2005 until their divorce. He has also been involved in various stage productions, including "The Three Sisters" and "Love's Labour's Lost" at the Royal Shakespeare Company. Throughout his career, Northam has demonstrated his versatility as a stage and screen actor, taking on a wide range of roles in film, television, and theatre.

title: Harry Cave
text:
Harry Cave was a New Zealand cricketer who played for his country in 19 Test matches, captaining the team in nine of them. Born on October 10, 1922, in the Wanganui area, Cave came from a family of farmers and cricketers. His father had a farm at Westmere, and his uncle Ken Cave umpired in New Zealand's first Test series in 1929-30. Cave attended Wanganui Collegiate School and took up farming after leaving school, often balancing his cricket career with his life on the farm.

Cave's cricket career began when he played for Wanganui in his teens, and he became one of their leading players in the Hawke Cup. He made his first-class debut for Wellington on Christmas Eve 1945, and in January 1947, he took 6 for 44 and 2 for 72 against Canterbury in the Plunket Shield. However, a torn elbow muscle in 1947 forced him to change his bowling style, relying on seamers, cutters, and in-swingers instead of his stock out-swinger.

Cave toured England in 1949 and played in all four Tests, with the tour report in Wisden describing his bowling as "always steady and reliable". However, he took only four wickets from 141 overs in the Tests at an average of 116.25. In the 1950s, Cave was one of the leading players in Central Districts' inaugural season in the Plunket Shield, and he captained the team to the Plunket Shield title for the first time in 1953-54.

Cave's Test career gained momentum in the mid-1950s, and he was appointed captain of the New Zealand team on an eight-Test tour of Pakistan and India from October 1955 to January 1956. The tour was a challenging one, with extreme heat, sub-standard accommodation and facilities, and dubious umpiring making it difficult for the New Zealanders to play at their best. Cave, however, remained diplomatic throughout, bowling more overs than any other player and losing about 11 kilograms in weight on the tour.

Upon the team's return to New Zealand, Cave was captain in the First Test against the West Indies, and he had his best Test figures in the Fourth Test in Auckland, taking four wickets in each innings to help New Zealand to its first Test victory. He was New Zealand's leading bowler when the Australians toured in 1956-57, taking 17 wickets in the three unofficial Tests.

Cave's personal life was also fulfilling, as he married Vonnie Anderson in 1951 and had two sons. He and his wife were keen camellia growers, and he developed a variety that was named after him. Cave passed away on September 15, 1989, at the age of 66, leaving behind a legacy as a dedicated cricketer and a true New Zealander. His wife, Vonnie, went on to be appointed a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit for services to photography and horticulture in 2009.

title: Isla Fisher
text:
Isla Fisher is an Australian actress born on February 3, 1976, in Muscat, Oman, to Scottish parents. Her family moved to Australia when she was six years old, and she grew up in Perth with her parents and four brothers. Fisher has described her upbringing as "great" and "very outdoorsy," and she has stated that her "sensibility is Australian" and that she has a "laid-back attitude to life." Her parents later separated, and her mother and brothers now live in Athens, Greece, while her father lives in Frankfurt, Germany.

Fisher began her acting career at a young age, appearing in television commercials and making her professional acting debut in 1993 with guest-starring roles in the children's television shows "Bay City" and "Paradise Beach." She gained prominence for her portrayal of Shannon Reed on the Australian soap opera "Home and Away" from 1994 to 1997, earning two Logie Award nominations for Most Popular New Talent and Most Popular Actress.

After leaving "Home and Away," Fisher enrolled at L'École Internationale de Théâtre Jacques Lecoq in Paris, where she studied clown, mime, musical theatre, and commedia dell'arte. She transitioned to Hollywood in 2002 with a supporting role in the comedy horror film "Scooby-Doo," which was a commercial success, grossing $275.7 million worldwide. Fisher's performance in the film helped her gain recognition in the industry, and she went on to appear in films such as "Wedding Crashers" (2005), "Wedding Daze" (2006), and "Definitely, Maybe" (2008).

Fisher's breakthrough role came in 2005 with the comedy "Wedding Crashers," which grossed $285.1 million worldwide and earned her the Best Breakthrough Performance Award at the 2006 MTV Movie Awards. She continued to appear in a range of films, including "The Lookout" (2007), "Hot Rod" (2007), and "Confessions of a Shopaholic" (2009). Fisher's performance in "Confessions of a Shopaholic" was well-received, and she received her third Teen Choice Award nomination.

In the 2010s, Fisher appeared in films such as "Burke and Hare" (2010), "Rango" (2011), and "Bachelorette" (2012). She voiced the Tooth Fairy in the animated film "Rise of the Guardians" (2012) and played the role of Myrtle MacQuigg in "The Great Gatsby" (2013). Fisher's performance in "The Great Gatsby" earned her nominations for Best Supporting Actress from the AACTA Awards, the Australian Film Critics Association, and the Film Critics Circle of Australia Awards.

Fisher also appeared in the heist thriller "Now You See Me" (2013) and the comedy-drama series "Arrested Development" (2013-2019). She starred in the independent horror film "Visions" (2015) and the action comedy films "Grimsby" (2016) and "Keeping Up with the Joneses" (2016). Fisher collaborated with her husband, Sacha Baron Cohen, in the British film "Grimsby," playing the handler of the best MI6 agent.

In addition to her acting career, Fisher is also a writer and has authored two young adult novels and the "Marge in Charge" book series. She married Sacha Baron Cohen in 2010, and the couple has three children together. Fisher has been involved in various charitable endeavors and has been recognized for her contributions to the entertainment industry.

Throughout her career, Fisher has demonstrated her versatility as an actress, taking on a range of roles in film and television. Her performances have been well-received by critics and audiences alike, and she has established herself as a talented and accomplished actress in Hollywood. With her laid-back attitude and great sense of humor, Fisher has become a beloved figure in the entertainment industry.

title: Rory Burns
text:
Rory Burns is an English cricketer born on August 26, 1990, in Epsom, Surrey. He has played internationally for the England Test cricket team and currently captains Surrey in first-class and List A cricket. Burns made his Test debut in 2018 and has since become a regular member of the England team. He has also led Surrey to multiple County Championship titles, including in 2018, 2022, 2023, and 2024.

Burns was educated at City of London Freemen's School, Whitgift School, and Cardiff Metropolitan University. He played Second XI cricket for both Surrey and Hampshire before making his first-class debut for Surrey in 2011. Burns made his first significant impact in the 2012 season, scoring a century against Leeds Bradford MCCU and filling in as wicket-keeper. He went on to establish himself as a regular opening batsman for Surrey, scoring 1000 runs in a season for the first time in 2014.

In 2015, Burns was involved in a serious collision with teammate Moisés Henriques during a NatWest t20 Blast game, which left both players unconscious and requiring medical attention. Despite the incident, Burns continued to play and finished the 2015 season with 1019 First-Class runs at an average of 48.52. He also played in several Royal London Cup games, scoring 364 runs.

In 2017, Burns made his highest score of 219 not out against Hampshire while deputizing as captain in place of the injured Gareth Batty. He was appointed club captain for first-class and List A formats in 2018, leading Surrey to their first County Championship title since 2002. Burns has since become known for his consistent batting, scoring over 1000 runs in a season for five consecutive years.

Burns's international career has been marked by several notable performances. He made his Test debut in 2018 against Sri Lanka and scored 155 runs in the series. He also played in the Ashes series against Australia, scoring 390 runs in 10 innings, including a maiden Test century. Burns has also played against New Zealand, South Africa, West Indies, and Pakistan, scoring several half-centuries and centuries.

In addition to his cricket career, Burns is a family man. He missed England's 2021 tour of Sri Lanka for the birth of his daughter and is close to his school and Surrey teammate Jason Roy, who has been his best man at his wedding.

Overall, Rory Burns is a talented and accomplished cricketer who has made a significant impact in both domestic and international cricket. His consistent batting and leadership skills have made him a valuable asset to Surrey and the England Test team. With his impressive record and dedication to the sport, Burns is likely to continue to be a key player in English cricket for years to come.

title: Andriy Yarmolenko
text:
Andriy Yarmolenko is a Ukrainian professional footballer who plays as a winger or forward for Dynamo Kyiv and captains the Ukraine national team. Born on October 23, 1989, in Leningrad, Russia, to Ukrainian parents, Yarmolenko moved to Ukraine with his family at a young age and grew up in Chernihiv. He began playing football at the age of 4-5 and was noticed by coach Mykola Lypoviy, who invited him to join the Youth Sports School "Yunist" in Chernihiv.

Yarmolenko's club career began at Chernihiv Youth Sports School "Yunist", from which he joined Dynamo Kyiv Youth Academy at the age of 13. However, he returned to Chernihiv after a year due to physical demands. He then played for several clubs, including Desna Chernihiv, Lokomotyv Kyiv, and Vidradnyi Kyiv, before joining Dynamo Kyiv's second team, Dynamo-2, in 2007. Yarmolenko made his debut for Dynamo Kyiv's first team in 2008 and quickly established himself as a talented young player, earning praise from journalists and coaches alike.

In 2017, Yarmolenko signed with Borussia Dortmund, making his debut in September of that year. A year later, he joined West Ham United, making his debut in August 2018. During his time at West Ham, Yarmolenko suffered several injuries, including an Achilles tear and an adductor muscle injury. Despite these setbacks, he continued to play for the club until the end of his contract in June 2022.

Yarmolenko has been a full international for Ukraine since 2009, scoring 46 goals in 125 matches and playing in several major tournaments, including the UEFA European Championship in 2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024. He has also been recognized for his individual achievements, including being named the Ukrainian Premier League Footballer of the Year and the Ukrainian Footballer of the Year.

In 2022, Yarmolenko returned to Ukraine, joining Al-Ain in the United Arab Emirates. However, he soon returned to Dynamo Kyiv, signing a two-year contract in June 2023. Off the pitch, Yarmolenko is a family man with three sons and has been involved in various charitable initiatives, including providing financial support to the Armed Forces of Ukraine during the Russian invasion.

Yarmolenko has also been recognized for his contributions to his hometown of Chernihiv, being elected an honorary citizen in 2021. He has also had a mural dedicated to him in the city and has had a competition, the Andriy Yarmolenko Cup, named in his honor. In 2024, Yarmolenko obtained his UEFA "A" coaching license, marking a new chapter in his football career. Throughout his career, Yarmolenko has demonstrated his commitment to his country, his team, and his community, making him a respected and beloved figure in Ukrainian football.

title: Thierry Henry
text:
Thierry Henry is widely regarded as one of the greatest players in football history, and many consider him to be the greatest player in Premier League history. Born on August 17, 1977, in Les Ulis, a suburb of Paris, Henry is of Antillean heritage, with his father from Guadeloupe and his mother from Martinique. He began playing football at a young age and joined Monaco in 1990, impressing scouts with his skills and scoring all six goals in a 6-0 win. Henry made his professional debut with Monaco in 1994 and quickly established himself as a talented young player, winning the French Young Footballer of the Year award in 1996.

In 1999, Henry transferred to Juventus, but he struggled to adapt to the Italian league and made only 16 appearances, scoring three goals. He attributed his struggles to disagreements with the club's director, Luciano Moggi. Later that year, he joined Arsenal, reuniting with his former manager Arsène Wenger, and quickly established himself as a world-class player. Henry made his name as a prolific striker, known for his finishing, elegance, dribbling, and close control, speed, and chance-creating.

During his time at Arsenal, Henry won the Premier League Golden Boot a record four times and was named the FWA Footballer of the Year a record three times. He also won three FA Cups and two Premier League titles with the club, including one during an unbeaten Invincible season. Henry became Arsenal's all-time leading scorer with 228 goals in all competitions and was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year a joint-record two times.

In 2007, Henry transferred to Barcelona, where he won La Liga, the Copa del Rey, and the UEFA Champions League in the 2008-09 season. He then joined Major League Soccer (MLS) club New York Red Bulls in 2010. Henry returned to Arsenal on loan from January to February 2012, before retiring in 2014.

Henry was also a key player for the French national team, winning the 1998 FIFA World Cup, UEFA Euro 2000, and 2003 FIFA Confederations Cup. He was named French Player of the Year a record five times and was included in the UEFA Euro 2000 Team of the Tournament. Henry retired from international football after the 2010 FIFA World Cup, having scored 51 goals in 123 appearances.

After retiring, Henry transitioned into coaching, beginning with Arsenal's youth teams in 2015. He then became an assistant coach for Belgium and later managed Monaco in 2018. Henry managed Montréal Impact in 2020 and led the team to the playoffs before departing in 2021. In 2023, he became the manager of the France national under-21 team and the France Olympic team, leading the team to a silver medal at the 2024 Summer Games.

Throughout his career, Henry received numerous individual accolades, including being named to the FIFA FIFPro World XI and the UEFA Team of the Year five times. He was also included in Pelé's list of the world's greatest living players, the FIFA 100. Henry's legacy as one of the greatest players of all time continues to be celebrated, and he remains involved in the sport as a coach and pundit.

title: James Theodore Bent
text:
James Theodore Bent was a prominent English explorer, archaeologist, and author of the 19th century. Born on March 30, 1852, in Liverpool, he was the son of James and Eleanor Bent, and his family was part of the wealthy Bent family, who owned Bent's Breweries. Bent's early life was marked by education at Malvern Wells preparatory school, Repton School, and Wadham College, Oxford, where he graduated in 1875. He developed a passion for travel and exploration, which would shape his future career.

In 1877, Bent married Mabel Hall-Dare, who became his companion, photographer, and diarist on all his travels. The couple spent nearly every year abroad, starting with extended travels in Italy and Greece. Bent's writing career began with the publication of "A Freak of Freedom" in 1879, a book about the republic of San Marino, for which he was made a citizen. He also wrote "Genoa: How the Republic Rose and Fell" and "Life of Giuseppe Garibaldi".

Bent's interests shifted towards archaeological and ethnographic research, particularly in the Eastern Mediterranean and Anatolia. His research in the Aegean archipelago led to the publication of "The Cyclades; or, Life among the Insular Greeks" in 1885. He conducted excavations in the Bahrein Islands, Cilicia Trachea, and Mashonaland, where he investigated the ruins of Great Zimbabwe. Bent believed that the Zimbabwe ruins were built by the ancestors of the Shona people, a view that was later supported by modern archaeologists.

Bent's expeditions took him to various parts of the world, including South Africa, Ethiopia, and southern Arabia. In 1893, he investigated the ruins of Axum in northern Ethiopia, and his book "The Sacred City of the Ethiopians" gives an account of this expedition. He also visited the Hadramut country, which was little known at the time, and studied its ancient history and physical features. During his travels, Bent collected hundreds of artefacts, which are now housed in museums such as the British Museum, the Pitt Rivers Museum, and the Victorian and Albert Museum.

Tragically, Bent's life was cut short when he contracted malarial fever during a journey in South Arabia and Socotra in 1896-1897. He died in London on May 5, 1897, just a few days after his return. His wife, Mabel, continued to publish their joint research, including "Southern Arabia, Soudan and Sakotra" in 1900. Bent's legacy as an explorer and archaeologist has endured, and his contributions to the field are still celebrated today. His notebooks and manuscripts are archived at various institutions, including the Hellenic Society in London, and have been digitized for public access.

title: Gary Woodland
text:
Gary Woodland is an American professional golfer born on May 21, 1984, in Topeka, Kansas. He grew up in the suburb of Tecumseh and attended Shawnee Heights High School. Woodland's athletic career began with basketball, for which he received a scholarship to play at Washburn University. However, he left after his freshman year to attend the University of Kansas on a golf scholarship. At KU, he studied sociology and had a successful college golf career, winning four tournaments.

After turning professional in 2007, Woodland played on the Nationwide Tour and later earned a spot on the PGA Tour through qualifying school in 2008. However, his debut season on the PGA Tour in 2009 was marred by struggles with form and a shoulder injury that cut his golfing year short. He made just eight cuts in 18 appearances that season. In 2010, Woodland divided his time between the PGA and Nationwide Tours, but continued to struggle for consistency, failing to record a single top-ten finish on either tour.

Woodland's breakthrough came in 2011 when he won his first PGA Tour title at the Transitions Championship. This victory secured his place at the 2011 Masters Tournament and elevated him to 53rd in the Official World Golf Ranking. He also won the Omega Mission Hills World Cup with Matt Kuchar in November 2011 and finished the year ranked 17th on the PGA Tour money list and 51st in the OWGR.

Over the next few years, Woodland continued to improve, reaching the final of the 2015 WGC-Cadillac Match Play and moving to a career-best 32nd in the OWGR. In 2018, he won his third PGA Tour event at the Waste Management Phoenix Open in a sudden-death playoff. Woodland also had a notable performance at the PGA Championship that year, leading by a stroke at the halfway stage before finishing in a tie for sixth.

However, it was in 2019 that Woodland achieved his greatest success. He held the lead entering the final round at the Sentry Tournament of Champions but finished in second place. That June, he won his first major championship at the U.S. Open, shooting a 2-under-par 69 to secure a three-shot victory over Brooks Koepka. This win moved him from 25th to 12th in the Official World Golf Ranking and marked his sixth professional victory.

In addition to his golf career, Woodland has been involved in several notable moments. In 2018, he invited Amy Bockerstette, a collegiate golfer with Down syndrome, to play the par-3 16th hole at TPC Scottsdale during a Tuesday practice round at the Waste Management Phoenix Open. A video of Bockerstette parring the hole went viral, receiving 43 million views across social media platforms. Woodland also FaceTimed Bockerstette live during his post-win press conference after his U.S. Open victory, telling her "I used your positive energy." He also appeared on The Today Show with Bockerstette, pointing to the U.S. Open trophy in her hands, saying "We won this together."

In 2019, Woodland played on the U.S. team at the Presidents Cup, which the U.S. won 16-14. He went 1-2-1 and lost his Sunday singles match against Im Sung-jae. In August 2023, Woodland revealed that he had been diagnosed with a brain lesion and underwent brain surgery in September 2023. In February 2025, he was awarded the PGA Tour Courage Award. Throughout his career, Woodland has demonstrated resilience and determination, both on and off the course.

title: Danny Faure
text:
Danny Faure, born on May 8, 1962, in the Ugandan town of Kilembe to Seychellois parents, is a Seychellois politician who served as the fourth President of Seychelles from October 16, 2016, to October 26, 2020. Prior to his presidency, Faure held various positions in the government, including Vice-President of Seychelles from 2010 to 2016. He is a member of the United Seychelles Party.

Faure completed his primary and secondary education in the Seychelles and later studied at the University of Havana in Cuba, graduating with a degree in political science. He began his career in 1985 as an assistant curriculum officer at the Seychelles education ministry, at the age of 23. He also worked as a lecturer at the National Youth Service and the Seychelles Polytechnic.

In 1993, following the return of multiparty democracy to Seychelles, Faure became the leader of government business in the National Assembly, a position he held until 1998. He was then appointed Minister of Education and went on to serve in various ministerial capacities, including youth, finance, trade and industries, public administration, and information and communication technology. In 2006, he was appointed Minister of Finance by President James Michel, overseeing economic reforms recommended by the International Monetary Fund.

Faure's rise to prominence continued as he was appointed Vice-President on July 1, 2010, while retaining the finance portfolio. In 2016, President James Michel announced his resignation, effective October 16, 2016, and transferred power to Faure, who was sworn in as the new President of Seychelles. As there were four years of Michel's term remaining, it was counted as a full term for Faure.

During his presidency, Faure made several notable appearances, including a speech from underwater, pleading for stronger protections for the world's oceans, and a visit to the United States, where he was awarded the National Geographic Society's prestigious 'Planetary and Leadership Award' in 2019. However, Faure's term as President came to an end on October 26, 2020, when he lost the presidential election to Wavel Ramkalawan.

In his personal life, Faure is a father of five children and married Shermin Rudie Bastienne on April 4, 2021. Throughout his career, Faure has demonstrated his commitment to public service and his country, serving in various capacities and advocating for the protection of the environment.

title: Kajal Aggarwal
text:
Kajal Aggarwal is a renowned Indian actress who has made a significant impact in the South Indian film industry, particularly in Telugu, Tamil, and Hindi films. Born on June 19, 1985, in Mumbai, Kajal was raised in a Punjabi family and completed her education in Mumbai. She studied at St. Anne's High School, Fort, Mumbai, and graduated in mass media with a specialization in marketing and advertising from Kishinchand Chellaram College.

Kajal began her acting career with a minor role in the 2004 Hindi film Kyun! Ho Gaya Na... and made her Telugu debut in 2007 with Lakshmi Kalyanam. However, it was her role in the 2007 film Chandamama that brought her wider recognition. Her breakthrough performance came in 2009 with the fantasy film Magadheera, which became one of the highest-grossing Telugu films of all time and earned her critical acclaim.

Throughout her career, Kajal has appeared in a range of successful films, including Darling, Brindavanam, Mr. Perfect, Businessman, Naayak, Baadshah, Govindudu Andarivadele, Temper, Khaidi No. 150, Nene Raju Nene Mantri, Awe, and Bhagavanth Kesari. She has also played the female lead in high-profile Tamil projects such as Naan Mahaan Alla, Maattrraan, Thuppakki, Jilla, Vivegam, and Mersal. Her most successful Hindi films include the action film Singham and the thriller Special 26.

Kajal has received numerous awards and nominations for her performances, including three SIIMA Awards and four Filmfare Awards South nominations. In 2020, a wax figure of her was put on display at Madame Tussauds Singapore, making her the first actress from South Indian cinema to receive this honor.

In her personal life, Kajal married Gautam Kitchlu in 2020, and the couple has a son named Neil, born in 2022. Kajal is considered one of the highest-paid actresses in South Indian cinema and has been recognized for her contributions to the film industry.

Throughout her career, Kajal has demonstrated her versatility as an actress, taking on a wide range of roles in different languages and genres. Her dedication to her craft and her ability to connect with audiences have made her a beloved figure in the South Indian film industry. With her continued success, Kajal remains one of the most popular and sought-after actresses in Indian cinema.

Kajal's recent projects include films like Acharya, Mosagallu, Mumbai Saga, Hey Sinamika, and Bhagavanth Kesari. She has also been announced to star in upcoming films like Sikandar, Kannappa, Indian 3, and The India Story. With her impressive filmography and numerous projects in the pipeline, Kajal Aggarwal continues to be a prominent figure in the Indian film industry.
